And the people who work in this industry, as in any other, live in the same city, but depending on who they are and how much they earn, they do very different things in that city.

correctItems.text: Like any industry, the workers there are part of unions.
For instance, the dancers, stunt artists and the extras are all part of a junior artists association, whose demands include 8 hours shifts, proper wages and safe working conditions.
The products of this industry are advertised and marketed through film distributors and cinema hall owners or through shops in the form of music cassettes and videos.
And the people who work in this industry, as in any other, live in the same city, but depending on who they are and how much they earn, they do very different things in that city.

correctItems.text: On the other hand, social institutions like caste, kinship networks, gender and region also influence the way that work is organised or the way in which products are marketed.
For instance, why do we find more women in certain jobs like nursing or teaching than in other sectors like engineering?
Is this just a coincidence or is it because society thinks that women are suited for caring and nurturing work as against jobs which are seen as 'tough' and masculine?
Yet nursing is physically much harder work than designing a bridge.
